paper_title: AI4Reading: Chinese Audiobook Interpretation System Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration
summary:
AI4Reading: Chinese Audiobook Interpretation System Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration - Minjiang Huang, Jipeng Qiang, Yi Zhu, Chaowei Zhang, Xiangyu Zhao, Kui Yu, 2025

AI4Reading targets automatic generation of Chinese audiobook interpretation content, a task that requires preserving source-book semantics while rewriting material into a more comprehensible, podcast-like spoken narrative. The technical objective is threefold: maintain factual and thematic fidelity to the book, improve accessibility of the explanation, and impose a coherent discourse structure suitable for long-form audio delivery. The system instantiates this objective as a multi-agent LLM pipeline coupled with speech synthesis, decomposing the generation process into 11 specialized agents that handle topic analysis, case analysis, editing, narration, and proofreading. The architecture operationalizes division of labor across agents so that thematic extraction, real-world example retrieval or construction, content reorganization, and spoken-style rewriting are performed as separate but coordinated stages rather than by a single monolithic generator. This design is positioned as a system demonstration at ACL 2025 and is explicitly built to output podcast-like audiobook interpretation scripts and synthesized speech rather than only text summaries. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23300?utm_source=openai))

The reported evaluation compares AI4Reading outputs against expert-produced interpretations. The main empirical finding is asymmetric quality across modalities: the generated interpretative scripts are described as simpler and more accurate than expert references, while speech generation quality still lags behind human-level narration. Publicly available metadata does not expose detailed benchmark tables, exact automatic metrics, or ablation numbers for individual agents, so the quantitative evidence visible from accessible sources is limited to this comparative conclusion rather than reproducible score breakdowns. What is concretely demonstrated, however, is an end-to-end system that transforms book content into structured Chinese interpretation scripts and synthesized audiobook-style output through coordinated agent roles, showing that multi-agent orchestration can improve script-level clarity and correctness even when downstream TTS naturalness remains the bottleneck. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23300?utm_source=openai))
